newsitem.title: JAPAN: NKorea representatives in Tokyo deny defection.
newsitem.headline: NKorea representatives in Tokyo deny defection.

text.p: North Korean representatives in Japan denied reports on Wednesday that a senior aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il had defected and was seeking asylum in South Korea.

"We confirmed with the North Korean embassy in Beijing that Secretary Hwang took a 4 p.m. train on Tuesday from Beijing to Pyongyang," a spokesman for the General Association of Korean Residents in Japan said, referring to Hwang Jang-yop, a secretary in North Korea's ruling Workers' Party.

The General Association of Korean Residents in Japan is the de-facto embassy of North Korea in Japan. Last week the association hosted a 13-day visit by Hwang to Japan. He left Tokyo for Beijing on Tuesday.
The South Korean government said earlier on Wednesday that Hwang and another North Korean had sought asylum at the South Korean embassy in China.

"Workers' Party secretary Hwang Jang-yop expressed intention to defect at 10:05 a.m. (0205 GMT) at the consular section of the embassy," said Ryu Kwang-sok, director-general of the South Korean Foreign Ministry's Asia-Pacific Bureau.

Hwang is one of 11 secretaries on the powerful secretariat of the Workers' Party. The secretariat includes Kim Jong-il, the son and political heir of North Korean founder Kim Il-sung who died in July 1994.
